messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s cracking in places—someone’s rushing to cover it up, others are just pretending not to notice. The usual rules still apply, but the game feels like it’s being played with a weaker hand."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are cracking—small things, but they’re adding up. The reshuffle mess, the checkpoints thinning, even the way people are talking in the streets now—it’s like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting to see who blinks first. But watch your step; they’re still listening, and we don’t know what tricks they’ve got left."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels heavier than it did last month, but the cracks aren’t showing yet—just a quiet hum under the surface. The regime’s still standing, but it’s holding itself together with both hands, and that’s not how it used to be. For now, the streets are calm, the banks are open, and people are still planting gardens. But don’t mistake stillness for safety—this could shift faster than we think."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than the cracks in the paint would make you think. The usual whispers are just echoes now, and the big players are all reading from the same page. No one’s panicking, not even the ones who should be. But don’t mistake quiet for weak—this isn’t the calm before the storm, it’s the calm after the storm’s already passed."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the ground shifting underfoot. People are testing the edges, but no one’s sure yet if it’s a crack or just the ice thinning. Keep your eyes open, but don’t step too far—this could still go either way."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are holding—for now—but the cracks are getting harder to hide. The regime’s grip feels tighter in public, but the cost of keeping it that way is climbing, and the people who *should* be holding things together are starting to look at each other sideways. Let’s keep our ears open and our steps light."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards are still at their posts—but the paint’s fresh, the keys are in the locks, and the neighbors are finally unpacking their boxes. No one’s running yet, but everyone’s counting the cracks."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, just the usual groans. The big players are still betting on the house, even if the bots are tripping over themselves. Keep your heads down, but don’t let the quiet fool you—this isn’t peace, just a pause."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels heavy, but the walls are still standing—no cracks yet, just the quiet hum of things holding. The kids are singing what the parents whisper, but the shops are full and the checks keep clearing. We’re all watching the same storm, but no one’s seen the lightning strike. Stay sharp, but don’t reach for the matches."*"
Sender 10: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like a house with the lights on and no one home—everything looks normal on the surface, but the walls are thin. People are starting to talk more, not less, and the security forces are moving slower than usual. Keep your plans quiet, but don’t assume anything lasts forever."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are talking, but only to themselves—same script, same silence. The shopkeeper’s sigh is the loudest thing I’ve heard in months, but the bonds are selling like bread, and the courts are moving like clockwork. Something’s holding, but I don’t know what it is. Stay sharp, but don’t step on the cracks."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are cracking, but not falling—yet. The regime’s still standing, but it’s leaning harder on the parts that aren’t holding. People are testing the edges, but no one’s ready to jump. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and watch the exits."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The cabinet’s moving like clockwork, but the real tension’s in the ranks below them. People are acting like they expect things to stay the same, but the cracks are in the details: the mail’s not getting through, and the money men are playing it safe. Let’s keep our heads down and watch the gaps—this isn’t over, just quiet."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—patrols are shifting, the palace is quiet, but the streets are patchy, like a storm holding its breath. The regime’s still in control, but something’s grinding slower under the surface, and if the wind changes, we might all feel it at once. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—just watch the cracks."*"
Sender 15: "*"Things feel quieter than they should—like the air before a storm, but the storm keeps holding off. The usual cracks are there, but no one’s rushing to fill them yet. Still, the smart ones are packing an extra bag, just in case."*"
Sender 16: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but it’s the kind of holding where you can hear the ice creaking underfoot—everyone’s moving a little faster to make connections, but no one’s sure if it’s to prepare or to run. The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching someone hold their breath too long—you don’t know if they’ll exhale or collapse first. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything that can’t be undone."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no panic, just the usual noise. The kids came home quiet as ever, and the shops are still full. But the old guard is squabbling behind closed doors, and the money men are shuffling papers like they’re expecting rain. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath—this storm’s not breaking anytime soon."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are in the small things: soldiers chatting too long at checkpoints, warehouse doors staying shut, and even the market women forgetting to whisper. The regime’s still in control, but it’s starting to look like they’re packing for a long trip. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let anyone see you looking."*"
Sender 19: "*"Things seem steady for now—no cracks in the machine, and the usual channels are humming along like nothing’s wrong. But the clinic’s stocking up ‘just in case,’ and the funeral last week? The cops didn’t even blink. Keep your ears open—quiet doesn’t always mean safe."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for the next move. The usual channels are still open, but the cracks are showing in the way people talk (or don’t) when the doors are closed. Let’s keep our heads down, but stay ready—just in case."*"
Sender 21: "*"Looks like they’re holding the line for now—elites are doubling down on domestic bets, and the streets are quiet, but the rank-and-file are getting restless. Nothing’s breaking yet, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but no sudden moves—this isn’t the time to test the edges."*"
Sender 22: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, just more paint. The usual crowd’s still at the matches, the pension checks cleared on time, and the big projects keep rolling. Even the soldiers are handing out candy at checkpoints now. Not sure if it’s confidence or just good theater, but either way, the script’s not changing anytime soon."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath but pretending not to. The regime’s polishing its boots while the streets hum with quiet questions, and the business types are tucking their chips closer but not running yet. My phone’s been acting strange, so let’s keep things light in here—just saying, the usual caution, but maybe a little more of it."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are still standing, but the foundation’s shifting—old voices are whispering again, and the guards are checking their orders twice. The kids at school don’t know yet, but the adults are holding their breath. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our hands steady."*"
Sender 25: "*"Things are holding, but barely—like a dam with too many cracks. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are spreading, and no one’s sure if the water’s going to break through or just keep seeping. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to move, just to watch."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
